items.text: Asks how the service sheds load when the email provider slows or throttles, including which messages are deferred first and how queue growth is bounded.
Checks whether the three independently delivered messages have separate idempotency and reconciliation behavior when one provider call succeeds and another fails.
Checks how the raw bearer token in a browser URL is protected from referrer, browser-history, analytics, and support-tool leakage.
Checks that the provider credential and public web origin come from deployment configuration with separate values and safe defaults for each environment.
Asks how a feature-flag rollback and a migration rollback preserve compatibility for outbox events and export-version consumers during a partial deploy.
Asks how focus and an announcement move to the relevant control after asynchronous validation so a screen-reader user knows that the server response changed the form.

weakAnswers: The design is clear and ready to build, with sensible API boundaries and a gradual rollout.
Consider scalability, monitoring, and security as usage grows.
The document covers the API, worker, client, export, migration, and verification plan.
Add more tests and keep the documentation updated as implementation proceeds.
